sources.title: Hannes Meinlschmidt, Optimization with Partial Differential Equations, complete lecture notes, Winter term 2022/23
sources.locator: Complete 65-page notes; §1.1, printed pp. 2–3, and §3.2, printed pp. 31–37 (PDF pp. 35–41), especially the PDE constraint qualification and adjoint equations at the end of the semilinear elliptic example.
sources.disposition: Read as a complete independent lecture-notes treatment of function-space PDE optimization, model assumptions, and adjoint/KKT construction. The local finite-dimensional formula is proved in the assigned lemma; the notes do not supply the finite-budget status wrapper or a global algorithm convergence claim.

contents.name: §1.1 general PDE-constrained and reduced problem formulations, with continuity, closedness, and differentiability assumptions stated separately
§3.2 elliptic PDE constraint qualification and the resulting state/adjoint KKT equations
contents.locator: Printed pp. 36–37, PDF pp. 40–41; complete argument from surjectivity of the state derivative through the adjoint equations.

contents.name: Existence and optimality conditions for infinite-dimensional problems
contents.reason: The assigned algorithm certifies finite discrete residual conditions and makes no existence or convergence assertion for a PDE-constrained minimizer.

sources.title: Michael Hinze, A Variational Discretization Concept in Control Constrained Optimization: The Linear-Quadratic Case
sources.locator: Complete 19-page paper; §§1–2, printed pp. 1–5, and §3, printed pp. 5–8. Theorem 2.4 and its complete proof use the stated approximation assumptions (2.3); the elliptic PDE application follows separately.
sources.disposition: Read as an independent finite-element treatment of linear-quadratic reduced objectives, adjoint-based optimality conditions, and mesh error. Its O(h^2) result is used only with its own Assumption 2.3 and is not imported as a generic mesh rate.

contents.name: §1 reduced linear-quadratic objective, adjoint gradient formula, and closed convex admissible controls
contents.locator: Printed pp. 1–2, including Theorem 1.2 and its stated variational inequality.

contents.name: Theorem 2.4 and complete proof of a mesh-dependent control error under Assumption 2.3
contents.locator: Printed pp. 3–5. The local example calculates its own finite mesh and optimizer difference; it does not assert the paper's rate.

contents.name: §3 linear elliptic finite-element application and regularity hypotheses

sources.title: Fernando Gaspoz, Christian Kreuzer, Andreas Veeser, and Winnifried Wollner, A Posteriori Error Analysis for Optimization with PDE Constraints
sources.locator: Complete 28-page paper; §2, equations (2.3)–(2.23), Theorem 2.1 and proof; §3.1, Theorem 3.1 and complete proof, printed pp. 7–9 (PDF pp. 7–8).
sources.disposition: Read as an independent residual/error treatment for linear-quadratic PDE control. Its residual-to-error bounds require the paper's stated inf-sup, continuity, regularization, and control/observation assumptions; they are not a universal implication from solver residuals.

contents.name: §2 quadratic PDE control model and reduced/rescaled optimality system
contents.locator: Printed pp. 3–7, equations (2.3)–(2.23), with the assumptions and constants used in Theorem 2.1.

contents.name: Theorem 3.1, complete residual-to-error proof for the reduced and rescaled optimality system
contents.locator: Printed pp. 8–9, equations (3.1)–(3.3). The proof uses the form identity and the two-sided continuity/inf-sup bounds.

contents.name: Mesh-dependent and regularization-dependent error channels
contents.locator: Introduction, printed pp. 1–2, and Theorem 3.1, printed pp. 8–9. The local example computes a separate exact operator difference and makes no asymptotic rate claim.
